assembly_instructions: Cast the 1.8 m by 1.8 m reinforced concrete pad and set the steel base plate and three guy-anchor blocks at 120 degrees on a 2.8 m modeled radius.
Bolt the lower tapered tower section to the base plate, install the access door, then stack the middle and upper tower sections using the two bolted flange collars.
Attach the low and high guy-wire collars, run each steel guy wire to its matching concrete anchor, and tighten the three turnbuckles until the tower is plumb.
Install the yaw bearing ring on the upper tower flange, fasten the open nacelle tray to the bearing, then add the side rails while leaving the roof panel exploded above the tray.
Mount the generator stator in the nacelle tray, fit the rotor drum and brake disc on the front shaft, install the brake caliper, then attach the hub spinner and three blade-root flanges.
Bolt the three tapered fiberglass blades and their flattened chord caps to the root flanges at true 120 degree spacing in the YZ rotor disc, then install the visible root fasteners.

Assemble the passive furling tail: bolt the port and starboard hinge plates to the rear nacelle tray, insert the hinge pin, attach the offset tail bracket, tail boom, tension spring and tail vane frame.
Install the anemometer mast, cup rotor and wind-direction vane on the open nacelle frame, and wire both sensors to the nacelle cut-out controller.
Route the rubber DC downlead down the outside of the tower through lower, middle and upper cable clips, then run the ground conduit into the opened battery shed.

Build the cutaway shed floor, rear wall, side posts and lifted roof, then wire the battery modules, copper bus bars, blocking diode, charge controller, display, inverter and AC outlet in inspection order.

info.japanese_name: 50 kW オープンソース風力タービン
info.english_name: Open Source Ecology 50 kW Wind Turbine
info.summary: Horizontal-axis, three-blade wind turbine on a guyed tower. Part of OSE's Global Village Construction Set as the renewable-electricity prime mover.
info.description: The OSE 50 kW wind turbine is a community-scale, three-blade horizontal-axis wind turbine (HAWT) published as part of the Global Village Construction Set. The rotor captures wind via three composite blades bolted to a central hub; the hub turns a direct-drive DC generator housed in an opened nacelle at the top of a guyed tower. A tail vane behind the nacelle aligns the rotor into the wind by weathervaning around a yaw bearing, with a visible offset hinge and spring link representing passive furling hardware. A cup anemometer and wind vane on the nacelle feed the cut-in/cut-out controller. Direct-current output flows down an externally clipped cable to a cutaway ground battery shed containing batteries, bus bars, a blocking diode, a charge controller, an inverter and an AC output. The tower is stabilized by three steel guy wires anchored in concrete blocks at 120 degrees around the base. OSE's documentation is released under CC BY-SA 4.0.
info.operator: OSE community builders and off-grid installations
info.status: Design / small-scale builds; 50 kW class is the roadmap target

facts.label: Configuration
facts.value: Three-blade horizontal-axis upwind turbine with passive free-yaw tail vane and visible offset furling hinge hardware

facts.label: Scene scale
facts.value: Approximately 0.3× real size; modeled tower height is 4.75 m to yaw bearing and total blade-tip height is ≈7.6 m

facts.label: Rotor
facts.value: Three blades, ≈2.55 m modeled radius from hub center to tip, set 120 degrees apart in the YZ rotor plane

facts.label: Blade model
facts.value: Each blade uses a 2.35 m tapered fiberglass spar plus a flattened chord cap to approximate an airfoil without hiding the hub fasteners

facts.label: Tower
facts.value: Three tapered tubular steel sections, 1.6 m + 1.5 m + 1.3 m high, with cable clips on each section

facts.label: Guying
facts.value: Three steel guy wires at 120 degree spacing on a 2.8 m modeled anchor radius

facts.label: Drivetrain
facts.value: Direct-drive DC generator with visible stator, rotor drum and brake disc; no gearbox

facts.label: Output path
facts.value: DC downlead to battery bank, blocking diode, charge controller and inverter in ground shed

facts.label: License
facts.value: OSE design documentation is CC BY-SA 4.0

parts.name: Reinforced Concrete Foundation Pad
parts.role: Main poured concrete pad that spreads tower compression load into the ground.

parts.name: Bolted Steel Tower Base Plate
parts.role: Square steel plate with anchor bolts that clamps the tower to the concrete pad.

parts.name: Lower Tapered Tower Tube
parts.role: Widest tubular tower section carrying base bending load and the service opening.

parts.name: Tower Access Door
parts.role: Removable hatch for reaching cable clamps and tower-base electrical service points.

parts.name: Lower Bolted Flange Collar
parts.role: Bolted ring joining the lower and middle tower tubes with visible assembly break.

parts.name: Middle Tapered Tower Tube
parts.role: Intermediate tubular section that provides height while reducing tower mass.

parts.name: Upper Bolted Flange Collar
parts.role: Bolted ring joining the middle and upper tower tubes for sectional construction.

parts.name: Upper Tapered Tower Tube
parts.role: Narrow top tower section that supports the yaw bearing and nacelle loads.

parts.name: Lower Guy-Wire Collar
parts.role: Clamp ring where the lower stabilizing guy wires attach to the tower.

parts.name: Upper Guy-Wire Collar
parts.role: Higher clamp ring that shares lateral tower load into the three guy wires.

parts.name: Guy Anchor A (+X)
parts.role: Concrete deadman anchor for the east guy wire at ground level.

parts.name: Guy Anchor B (120 degrees)
parts.role: Concrete deadman anchor for the second guy wire on the 120 degree radial.

parts.name: Guy Anchor C (240 degrees)
parts.role: Concrete deadman anchor for the third guy wire on the 240 degree radial.

parts.name: Guy Turnbuckle A
parts.role: Adjustable tensioner that tightens the +X guy wire after tower erection.

parts.name: Guy Turnbuckle B
parts.role: Adjustable tensioner that tightens the 120 degree guy wire at its concrete anchor.

parts.name: Guy Turnbuckle C
parts.role: Adjustable tensioner that tightens the 240 degree guy wire at its concrete anchor.

parts.name: Steel Guy Wire A
parts.role: Tension cable from the tower guy collars to the +X anchor block.

parts.name: Steel Guy Wire B
parts.role: Tension cable from the tower guy collars to the 120 degree anchor block.

parts.name: Steel Guy Wire C
parts.role: Tension cable from the tower guy collars to the 240 degree anchor block.

parts.name: Yaw Bearing Ring
parts.role: Horizontal thrust bearing that lets the nacelle rotate freely into the wind.

parts.name: Open Nacelle Tray
parts.role: Cutaway lower nacelle shell that supports the drivetrain while leaving internals visible.

parts.name: Port Nacelle Side Rail
parts.role: Low side wall of the opened nacelle that shows the generator instead of hiding it.

parts.name: Starboard Nacelle Side Rail
parts.role: Opposite low side wall of the opened nacelle for the cutaway assembly view.

parts.name: Exploded Removable Nacelle Roof
parts.role: Removed roof panel displayed above and to the port side so the nacelle internals stay visible.

parts.name: Direct-Drive Generator Stator
parts.role: Stationary copper winding pack that produces DC output without a gearbox.

parts.name: Permanent-Magnet Rotor Drum
parts.role: Rotating magnet drum fixed to the blade shaft and visible ahead of the stator.

parts.name: Rotor Brake Disc
parts.role: Flat mechanical brake disc on the rotor shaft for shutdown and overspeed restraint.

parts.name: Brake Caliper
parts.role: Clamp body that grips the brake disc during service shutdown.

parts.name: Nacelle Cut-Out Controller
parts.role: Small controller box that reads wind sensors and commands electrical cut-out.

parts.name: Rotor Hub Spinner
parts.role: Aerodynamic nose cone and central hub where the three blade roots bolt on.

parts.name: Blade Root Flange Top
parts.role: Round bolted flange transferring the top blade load into the hub.

parts.name: Blade Root Flange Lower Port
parts.role: Bolted flange for the blade angled down toward the port side of the rotor disc.

parts.name: Blade Root Flange Lower Starboard
parts.role: Bolted flange for the blade angled down toward the starboard side of the rotor disc.

parts.name: Top Root Bolt A
parts.role: Visible fastener head showing how the top blade root is bolted to the hub flange.

parts.name: Top Root Bolt B
parts.role: Second visible fastener head on the top blade root flange.

parts.name: Port Root Bolt A
parts.role: Visible fastener head on the lower-port blade root flange.

parts.name: Port Root Bolt B
parts.role: Second visible fastener head on the lower-port blade root flange.

parts.name: Starboard Root Bolt A
parts.role: Visible fastener head on the lower-starboard blade root flange.

parts.name: Starboard Root Bolt B
parts.role: Second visible fastener head on the lower-starboard blade root flange.

parts.name: Tapered Fiberglass Blade Top Spar
parts.role: Upper tapered composite blade spar running radially upward from root to tip.

parts.name: Flattened Airfoil Chord Top
parts.role: Thin flattened chord surface beside the top spar so the blade reads as an airfoil rather than a rod.

parts.name: Tapered Fiberglass Blade Lower Port Spar
parts.role: Lower blade spar angled down and toward +Z at 120 degrees in the rotor disc.

parts.name: Flattened Airfoil Chord Lower Port
parts.role: Thin chord panel aligned with the lower-port blade to show blade width and pitch.

parts.name: Tapered Fiberglass Blade Lower Starboard Spar
parts.role: Lower blade spar angled down and toward -Z at 240 degrees in the rotor disc.

parts.name: Flattened Airfoil Chord Lower Starboard
parts.role: Thin chord panel aligned with the lower-starboard blade to show blade width and pitch.

parts.name: Passive Furling Port Hinge Plate
parts.role: Port-side hinge lug bolted to the rear nacelle tray for the offset furling tail.

parts.name: Passive Furling Starboard Hinge Plate
parts.role: Starboard-side hinge lug completing the clevis for the passive furling tail boom.

parts.name: Furling Hinge Pin
parts.role: Horizontal pin through the clevis plates that lets the tail boom fold during high wind.

parts.name: Offset Tail Bracket
parts.role: Offset bracket that places the tail boom behind the furling hinge instead of rigidly on the nacelle centerline.

parts.name: Rear Tail Boom
parts.role: Rear spar that places the tail vane far enough aft to weathervane the rotor.

parts.name: Tail Furling Return Spring
parts.role: Tension spring linking nacelle tray to tail bracket so the tail recenters after furling.

parts.name: Tail Vane Frame
parts.role: Vertical frame member that carries the fiberglass tail fin.

parts.name: Fiberglass Tail Vane Panel
parts.role: Broad vertical fin that passively yaws the nacelle into the wind.

parts.name: Anemometer Mast
parts.role: Vertical instrument mast mounted on the nacelle frame above the cutaway tray.

parts.name: Anemometer Cup Cross Arm
parts.role: Small rotor arm holding the three wind-speed cups around the mast.

parts.name: Anemometer Cup 1
parts.role: Hemispherical cup approximated as a sphere that catches wind for speed sensing.

parts.name: Anemometer Cup 2
parts.role: Second visible wind cup completing the rotating anemometer silhouette.

parts.name: Anemometer Cup 3
parts.role: Third visible wind cup completing the wind-speed sensor assembly.

parts.name: Wind Vane Pivot
parts.role: Vertical pivot post for the small wind-direction arrow beside the anemometer.

parts.name: Wind-Direction Vane Arrow
parts.role: Small horizontal arrow that reports wind direction to the controller.

parts.name: Exterior DC Downlead Cable
parts.role: Insulated DC cable running down the outside of the tower from generator to ground electronics.

parts.name: Lower Cable Clip
parts.role: Clamp holding the DC downlead against the lower tower section.

parts.name: Middle Cable Clip
parts.role: Clamp holding the DC downlead against the middle tower section.

parts.name: Upper Cable Clip
parts.role: Clamp holding the DC downlead near the upper tower section.

parts.name: Ground DC Cable Conduit
parts.role: Low conduit carrying the tower downlead across the ground into the open battery shed.

parts.name: Battery Shed Floor Plate
parts.role: Small equipment-pad floor for the ground-level battery and inverter assembly.

parts.name: Cutaway Battery Shed Back Wall
parts.role: Rear wall left standing while the front and one side are removed to reveal the electrical gear.

parts.name: Battery Shed Front Sill
parts.role: Low front sill marks the removed front wall without blocking the view of batteries and bus bars.

parts.name: Battery Shed Left Corner Post
parts.role: Exposed corner post showing the shed frame while keeping the side open for inspection.

parts.name: Battery Shed Right Corner Post
parts.role: Opposite exposed corner post supporting the lifted roof reference plane.

parts.name: Exploded Battery Shed Roof
parts.role: Removable roof panel lifted above the shed so the battery bank remains visible.

parts.name: Battery Module 1
parts.role: First visible battery block storing DC energy from the wind turbine.

parts.name: Battery Module 2
parts.role: Second visible battery block wired in the ground-level DC storage bank.

parts.name: Positive Copper Bus Bar
parts.role: Copper positive bus tying both battery modules to the charge controller.

parts.name: Negative Copper Bus Bar
parts.role: Copper negative return bus tying both battery modules to the inverter circuit.

parts.name: Blocking Diode Heat Sink
parts.role: Heat-sunk blocking diode preventing the battery bank from back-driving the generator.

parts.name: Charge Controller
parts.role: Wall-mounted controller that regulates turbine DC input before the battery bank and inverter.

parts.name: Controller Glass Display
parts.role: Small readout on the charge controller for voltage, current and fault state.

parts.name: Inverter Box
parts.role: DC-to-AC inverter mounted on the opened shed wall for conditioned electrical output.

parts.name: AC Output Receptacle
parts.role: Visible output interface showing where conditioned AC power leaves the inverter.
